meta.parties: Nizam v. Mustaffa (S. C. 41/80) Mustaffa v. Nizam(S. C. 53/80)

rules.statement: Where the dominant or primary intention of the parties to a transaction is to effect a lease of a business, then the fact that the lessee of that business has a personal privilege of occupying the land on which the business is being conducted does not give the lessee any interest affecting land such as to require notarial execution in terms section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance.
rules.supporting_quote: "It seems clear that where the dominant or primary intention of the parties to a transaction is to effect a lease of a business, then the fact that the lessee of that business has a personal privilege of occupying the land on which the business is being conducted, albeit exclusively, does not give the lessee any interest affecting land such as to require notarial execution."
